quote: SnSe is a promising thermoelectric material with a ultralow lattice thermal conductivity below 1 W/mK at room temperature.
Sn vacancies can significantly modulate the carrier concentration in SnSe, shifting the Fermi level toward the valence band.
First-principles calculations predict a formation energy of -0.2 eV for Se vacancies, suggesting they are thermodynamically favored.
Experimental synthesis shows severe phase separation above 5% Se vacancy concentration, inconsistent with single-phase assumptions.
The lattice thermal conductivity of SnSe single crystals is around 0.8 W/mK at 300 K, among the lowest reported for crystalline solids.
Sn vacancies are far less studied than Se vacancies for thermoelectric optimization, leaving a largely unexplored design space.
Early DFT studies overestimated the stability of vacancy-ordered phases; later experiments revealed decomposition below the predicted temperatures.
